experiment.objective: Search model families, hyperparameters, feature arms and targets in four controlled stages to find the strongest configuration that survives costs, turnover, overfitting diagnostics and a multiple-testing correction scaled to the size of the search itself.
notes: Staged search. The budget is declared in src/quant/study/search.py and selected at the command line; it is recorded in the artifact.
A larger budget raises the significance bar rather than lowering it. The `survives_search_size` gate makes that explicit.
Selection uses validation folds only. The 252-session holdout is reserved before any fold is cut and the firewall refuses its rows.
The best possible outcome is DEVELOPMENT CANDIDATE. Promotion remains blocked until the holdout is spent under the contract.
NO PRODUCTION CANDIDATE is a valid and complete result.

budget.name: overnight
budget.description: A full night. The largest budget this project's trial accounting will carry.

projection.note: Upper bound: the projection assumes the most expensive families advance from the screen. Costs are EXP-006's measured per-config timings scaled by feature count.

multiple_testing_cost.interpretation: A search of 879 configurations raises the cumulative count to 1035. The best of 1035 zero-skill configurations would be expected to show |t| ~ 3.39, so a finding must clear that before it is interesting, and ~4.06 to clear Bonferroni at 5%.

multiple_testing.interpretation: A search of 873 configurations raises the cumulative count to 1029. The best of 1029 zero-skill configurations would be expected to show |t| ~ 3.38, so a finding must clear that before it is interesting, and ~4.06 to clear Bonferroni at 5%.

checks.detail: universe does not declare point-in-time membership — any study over it is survivorship-biased and must be labelled so
no feature correlates with any label above 0.999

notes: observation stride 5 sessions, applied after feature computation so lookback windows remain in trading days
21 symbol(s) skipped for fewer than 260 sessions
cross-sectional columns (_xs) normalised within point-in-time universe membership only; names outside the universe on a date carry NULL there
macro features carry a one-session availability lag applied at source
8 option feature(s) attached as-of (latest snapshot at or before each date, 21-day staleness cap)
4 earnings feature(s) attached from the announcement's availability date, honouring before-open vs after-close; periods with no matching announcement are dropped

universe.name: liquid
notes: Liquidity-ranked, not index membership. Do not describe a study over this universe as an index backtest.
Survivorship-free by construction: membership is selected from each month's whole-market cross-section, so names that later delisted are present in the months they were liquid.
Screens: non-ETF, non-test-issue, close >= 5.0, top 250 by 3-month trailing-median dollar volume (trailing window only), dropped after symbol.last_seen.
coverage_class is 'partial' before 2017-10-26, where symbol.last_seen has no data and delisting is inferred only from a name leaving the cross-section.

holdout.note: Reserved before any fold was cut; the firewall refuses its rows.
